free_tier.stated: 25 hours of complimentary cloud credit, stated as approximately USD 50: 'AMD is offering an initial 25 hours of complimentary cloud credit to qualified developers who apply and are accepted.' The credit is valid for 10 days from deposit, covers AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs only, and excludes attached volumes, object storage and backups. A card is required at account creation.

retention.stated: Two destruction triggers and one that bills silently: expiry or exhaustion destroys the VM and its data, while a powered-off instance keeps consuming credit until it is destroyed, so stopping the machine does not stop the meter.

record.chaining: Twenty-five hours on one MI300X with 192 GB of VRAM is a real fine-tuning window, and it composes with nothing that needs to persist, because the VM and its disk are destroyed at the end of the credit.

identity_cost.detail: a valid credit card is required at the time of account creation and is required to access any complimentary cloud hours; the application is reviewed by AMD, and an expired or invalid card forfeits access to the GPUs and the data on them. AMD publishes no hold amount and no prepaid or virtual card rule: the card is entered on the hosting platform, which the vendor names as a third-party cloud with DigitalOcean support, and that platform's billing documentation sets the hold and the card types.

record.notes: Two clauses decide how a run has to be built. First, a powered-off instance still consumes credit, so the correct discipline is to destroy and not to stop, and a reader who stops a machine to save credit loses the credit anyway. Second, expiry destroys the data, so every artefact has to be copied out before the clock ends. The allocation is also discretionary, and the larger public grant is restricted to Indian researchers and startups, which is a country gate on the 100,000-hour figure. As of 2026-10-23 the page states 25 hours and 10 days; the earlier USD 100 over 30 days figure is wrong on both the amount and the window.

free_tier.stated: Node-hour allocations on a cluster of dual EPYC hosts with Instinct accelerators, awarded quarterly by proposal, reachable over SSH at hpcfund.amd.com with Slurm. The vendor states: 'Node-hour based allocations are awarded quarterly to proposal submissions supporting innovative, impactful, open-source AI and HPC research', and 'Successful proposals receive cluster access for up to one year'. The enrollment page closes the loop: 'Membership is open exclusively to faculty and researchers at universities and research institutions worldwide. Enroll using your official academic email address - personal emails won't qualify.'

record.notes: Classified as the academic half of AMD's program so the next reader does not confuse it with the 25-hour developer credit, which is a different door on a different site with a different amount. The institution condition is stated three times across three AMD pages, including the enrollment rule that personal email addresses will not qualify, which is the clearest statement of the gate found in this class. A fourth page states the cluster is reviewed by an internal team at the end of each quarter and requires an annual survey and publication notification. Worth noting for completeness: the cluster is reachable over SSH and runs Slurm, so the constraint is purely the door, not the tooling.
